Stavoren (port locode NLSTA), aka Starum, is an IJsselmeer (Lake IJssel) cruise port and town in the Netherlands' Friesland/Frisia province, with population around 1,000. A regularly scheduled passenger ferry service links Stavoren with Enkhuizen, with an increased number of crossings to serve the tourists during summer.

The town was founded in the 8th-century and received city rights in the mid-11th-century (making it Frisia's oldest). A flood submerged the entire town in 1657.

Marina Stavoren cruise port

Marina Stavoren Inner Harbour is a dock and premium boat berthing facility serving leisure boats, luxury yachts, and river cruise ships due to its unique location between IJsselmeer and Frisia's scenic lakes. Marina Stavoren is also a cruise port for riverboats cruising the area on roundtrips from Germany. Day boat tours are also provided as roundtrips from Stavoren to the Wadden Islands or to Enkhuizen, Medemblik, Sneek, Heeg, Woudsend, IJlst.

As facilities, Marina Stavoren provides premium berths (boat mooring piers), shoreside power, freshwater supply, diesel fueling station, Graywater pumping station, wastewater storage tanks, sanitary rooms, combined shop (watersports/supermarket), laundrette (self-service laundry room), gym room, outdoor playground, indoor swimming pool and playground (both free of charge), car parking (within the harbor), security (CCTV surveillance).

As a cruise port, Stavoren was included in the 2020 schedule of the Nicko Cruises-operated ship Alemannia.
